newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open unchanged to $5 higher Wednesday on the heels of a firm performance in London overnight, traders said.

LIFFE cocoa futures rose as sterling's weakness helped the market defy lower pre-opening expectations. At the midday break, September was up 13 stg at 1,014 stg a tonne, traded 1,015 to 1,003 stg. December rose 11 stg to 1,044 stg.
But some traders in New York said strength in the dollar against Sterling and other European currencies was likely to weigh on the market.
"Based on currency, I'm calling September down $5," said one trader. "Those calling it higher are just hopeful longs."

Tuesday, New York cocoa futures ended broadly lower for the second straight session, pressured by speculative liquidation. September settled down $17 at $1,483 a tonne after ranging between $1,504 and $1,481. December closed $17 lower at $1,529, while the back months ended down $15 to $17.

Technically, dealers pegged September support near $1,480, with a breach of that level expected to lead to sell-stops believed to be building below $1,475. On the upside, traders were eyeing the $1,500 mark.
